CHOLANGITIS.title: Cholangitis (infection of the bile ducts)

items: Cholangitis is an infection of the bile ducts, the tubes that carry bile from the liver to the gut.
It is usually caused by a blockage, such as a stone or narrowing.
Upper right belly pain, fever or shaking chills, and yellow skin (jaundice).
Charcot's triad (pain, jaundice and fever with rigors) is present in about 7 in 10 people.
Blood cultures and liver function tests.
Ultrasound of the belly, and MRCP or CT if the ultrasound is not clear.
A bile sample at the time of a procedure to drain or treat the duct.
The blockage usually needs a procedure to drain the duct. Your team will decide.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not delay coming to hospital if you have fever with jaundice.
Tell your team about any past gallstone attacks.
Your team may check blood tests and scans after drainage.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with shaking chills, jaundice, or belly pain together
Low blood pressure, confusion or drowsiness
